Creation is wall time for the entire batch, excluding first status. Create + first status adds each successful worktree's first `git status`, run one at a time after all creates; the README summary and its multipliers use it. Values are medians of recorded rounds; one round is an observation, not a stable estimate. Allocation is additional filesystem-allocated MiB after first status, including indexes, staging and APFS metadata. Ranges retain observed allocator variation, not confidence intervals. Multipliers use unrounded point estimates. Missing measurements are not zeros; logical size and du do not measure exclusive APFS allocation.

- git-twig 0.6.0, built from 77db979 on each platform: Linux candidate SHA-256 7c7df4185a2b…, Windows d1f09377c34a…. Raw runs record the full hashes, Git binaries, input trees and harness commits.
- Original v0.4 input pins. Each workload/backend gets a fresh filesystem image, a seed checkout and a warmup; three paired rounds, one create at a time. Every measured create is verified independently: raw bytes, executable modes, symlink targets, native Twig cloning and an unchanged source after private writes. No failed create is retried silently.
- Linux: Threadripper 2990WX, Ubuntu 26.04 host kernel 7.0.0-43, Git 2.53.0 in a disposable ubuntu:26.04 container; XFS (reflink=1) and Btrfs loopback images on NVMe. Allocation is the filesystem's used space after the first status, including metadata, logs and shared extents counted once.
- Windows: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300 VM (16 vCPUs) on the same host, Git for Windows 2.56.0; fresh ReFS Dev Drive VHDX images. ReFS keeps committing volume changes for tens of seconds, so space is the file data clusters files reference, block-cloned clusters counted once. Files ReFS keeps resident in its metadata (Workers starter's are all small) have no clusters for either backend. The Linux kernel is not measured on Windows: it has paths that differ only in case.
- Time is creation plus each new worktree's first `git status`. 0.6 writes a verified index during creation, so its first status no longer rehashes every file: on macOS, OpenClaw takes longer to create than with 0.5 but is ready sooner.
- OpenClaw is pinned at 410c0dda40702e25263b49b8b7d0786a5e49e366 with its text=auto eol=lf attributes unchanged. Pulumi docs uses the full-history object store at 430261138aa08539cd598b9269bfe8f82fd49b78 with its markdown eol=lf rules unchanged. No code from either project was executed.
- Earlier campaigns (v0.3–v0.5) stay under bench/results with their own manifests and are indexed in bench/results/index.json; none is shown here as a 0.6 result.
